source: Apache Commons Collections GitHub Pull Request and source history
technology: Apache Commons Collections / Java / map decorators and collection views
error_description: Expired entries may remain visible when a PassiveExpiringMap is wrapped in Collections.synchronizedMap and callers reuse entrySet, keySet, or values views; removals through iterators may also leave bookkeeping state inconsistent.
i_base: PassiveExpiringMap removes expired entries through removeAllExpired and related expiration checks.
Collections.synchronizedMap supplies synchronized collection views and can cache views obtained from the wrapped map.
PassiveExpiringMap exposes entrySet, keySet, and values, each of which has expiration-related side effects.
The map keeps expiration times in a separate expirationMap that must be updated when entries are removed through collection views.
The fix adds custom collection-view decorators and iterators and adds tests for cached views, expiration, and iterator removal.

ccdg.details: View caching can route later calls to wrapper views rather than the map's own view methods.
Direct access to map views invokes cleanup.
Iterator removals must update the internal expiration index.
Missed cleanup leaves expired entries visible through a wrapper.

ground_truth.entity: cached collection views and expirationMap bookkeeping
ground_truth.operation: entrySet, keySet, values access and iterator removal

software_twin_snapshot.observed_failure_signal: An expired entry remained visible through a synchronized map view on the pinned pre-fix revision.
